name: Week 21 KB Conditioning — Thursday, Flow + Coordination Block (Spotlight: Figure-8 March)
description:
KB Thursday, full template, kept light on the legs so Friday legs stays strong — but it remains the right home for the heavier UPPER-BODY push (three days fresh off Monday, and it costs Friday nothing). **Warmup reminder:** halo → bottoms-up press (18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane) → internal core fist rotation → protective behind-back shrug, then the 7-move banded shoulder prep.

The Flow + Coordination block rotates to the **figure-8 march** — the figure-8 weave you already own, now walked. The press-to-march moves off this day entirely; it belongs to the GymFiesta circuit, which now runs whole on Tuesday. Mobility maintenance rotates its cue focus to the **TGU checkpoints**. The rest holds: strict press 50 at the 8s you earned, rows at 40, the canonical Bent Press Flow kept light, a balance closer, cooldown.

dayOverview.theme: Thursday KB day, full template, light on the LEGS so Friday legs stays fresh — but still the home for heavier UPPER push. Flow + Coordination rotates to the figure-8 march (the weave you own, now walked — coordination under load, no leg cost). Mobility maintenance rotates its cue focus to the TGU checkpoints. Strict press holds 50 at 8s, rows at 40. Conditioning + skill + balance — never a metabolic finisher.

spotlights.why: Rotates in from the pool. You already own the figure-8 weave — this adds locomotion to it, which is the hardest version of the same coordination problem: the bell has to keep its path through the legs while the legs are themselves moving. Pure coordination and core, essentially zero leg cost, which is the Thursday brief exactly. It also replaces the press-to-march, which has gone back to the GymFiesta circuit on Tuesday where it belongs.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Flow + Coordination block (permanent): W18 halo → reverse lunge · W19 split-stance pass-through · W20 single-arm press-to-march · W21 figure-8 march (current) · W22 halo → reverse lunge or a fresh weave. Mobility maintenance cue-focus rotates: W19 windmill → W20 bent press → W21 TGU checkpoints (current) → W22 windmill refresh.
watchpoints: **The press-to-march is gone from this day.** It's move #4 of the GymFiesta circuit, which now runs whole on Tuesday — so it isn't running in two places, and this day gets a real coordination move of its own instead of a borrowed one.

**Thursday is still the home for heavier UPPER PUSH** — three days fresh off Monday's push and it doesn't tax Friday legs, so it's effectively a second weekly push exposure. Load the strict press / bent press freely here; keep the LEGS light (Bent-Press-Flow squat/lunge + the balance closer stay light).

**Figure-8 march spotlight — the weave, now walking.** Light bell. Weave the bell through the legs in a figure-8 while STEPPING forward — the pass happens under a moving leg, so the hand-off has to be exact or the bell hits a shin. Slow and deliberate beats fast and scrappy. Zero leg load; it's a coordination piece, not conditioning.

**Strict overhead press holds 50 at 8/8/8.** W20 hit the 8s and it was 'kind of hard' — that's the floor rising. Hold 50, hold the reps clean, don't chase further. Strict (no push-press), pack the shoulder down, ribs down, both sides to the same standard.

**Mobility maintenance = TGU checkpoint refresh this week** — the get-up gets the sharper cues (pause at EVERY checkpoint, eyes on the bell throughout, the arm stays locked vertical the whole way). Bent press + windmill drop back to light maintenance.
**Right shoulder watch on the overhead work** (press, bent press, TGU lockout) — if it talks, lighten and slow down; back off range before grinding.
**Bottoms-up press stays in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane (T-plane light). Rotator-cuff prep.
**Protective shrug greasing set in the warmup** — 1 light set, DBs or a bell behind the body. Cheap, easy to forget.
**Balance closer, not a metabolic finisher** — single-leg RDL → bird-dog → standing side-to-side twist, light bell. Thursday is conditioning + skills + balance, and Friday legs is tomorrow.

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 15-20lb. Slow circles, both directions. Shoulder loosener — and the warm-up for the day's coordination work.

**LOAD:** 18lb. Bell inverted over a vertical forearm, grip HARD, shoulder packed. **8/side in two planes:** forward press + T-press. **Keep the T-plane lighter.** Rotator-cuff prep before the overhead work.
Standing, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — wakes the grip and forearms for the figure-8 hand-offs.

exercises.equipment: light DB pair or a kettlebell held behind the body
exercises.notes: **Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs nothing, easy to forget.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~3 min)

exercises.notes: Mini-band overhead OR blue rope band gripped in hands.
Elbows drive to the ribs, scaps depress.
Press out to a T — fires rear delts and mid-traps.
Pull apart at the sternum, scaps retract, ribs down.
Sweep the arms back. Don't overarch.
15s each side. Primes the lateral hinge for the bent press + windmill.
Both arms in a V/Y overhead. Hold and breathe — lower traps fire, primes the strict press and the TGU lockout.

sets.notes: 1 round of all 7 banded moves (~3 min). Sustained tension, no rest between positions.

sets.name: 🔆🌀 Flow + Coordination (permanent block — Spotlight: Figure-8 March)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 15-20lb. Slow halos to groove the shoulders before the weave.

**LOAD:** ~20-30lb (LIGHT — coordination, not load). 3 rounds.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the weave you own, now walking:**
- **Weave the bell through the legs in a figure-8 while STEPPING FORWARD** — the pass happens under a moving leg, which is what makes it hard
- **The hand-off has to be exact** — a lazy pass hits a shin; that's the feedback
- **Stay low and hinged, chest up** — don't stand tall between passes, the bell should never stop
- **Slow and deliberate beats fast and scrappy** — the skill is the timing of the hand-off against the step, not the pace
- **Ribs down, core braced** — the bell wants to pull the torso around; don't let it
- Zero leg load — this is a coordination piece, not conditioning. Keep it light and clean.

**Reflection:** does the bell keep a continuous path while the feet move, or do you find yourself pausing the walk to complete the pass? Continuous bell + continuous feet is the win.

sets.notes: **Permanent Flow + Coordination block.** Base KB skill-building — light bell, coordination and core, no leg cost. A familiar halo to warm up, then this week's chain (figure-8 march). 3 rounds, ~5 min, short rest. Keep it light and clean; it precedes the strength + flow work and shouldn't fatigue anything.

sets.name: Strength Block (Rows + Strict Press — the Heavy-Upper Slot)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 40lb. 8 each side. Hips hinged, back flat, pull the elbow to the hip. Slow on the way down.

**LOAD:** 50 across all sets — strict single-arm press (clean to rack, press straight up, NO push-press). W20 hit 8/8/8 at 50 and it was 'kind of hard' — hold 50, hold the 8s clean. The floor rose; own it before climbing off it.
- **Strict, not push-press** — the shoulder presses it
- **Ribs DOWN** before the press — no rib flare
- **Bicep finishes by the ear, full lockout, pack the shoulder DOWN**
- Slow descent back to the rack; **both sides to the same standard** — press the left as clean as the right.

sets.notes: Strength block — single-arm row + strict press. Thursday is the fresh-upper-push slot, so load the press; the legs stay light elsewhere. 3 sets. ~5 min.

sets.name: Bent Press Flow (Light Groove — Skill Practice)

exercises.notes: Bell starts on the floor between the feet, hips drive the lift, catch in the rack with the knees slightly bent.
Goblet/rack position. **LIGHT** — Friday legs is tomorrow, keep depth without grinding. Sit tall, full depth, no bouncing.
Stride out wide, sit into the working leg, keep the other leg long. Mobility, not strength.

The deliberate leverage move inside the flow — **the body goes DOWN, the bell barely moves.** From the rack, hinge and rotate AWAY from the bell side, eyes tracking the bell, until the arm locks out overhead. You lower your body under the bell; you don't press it up. Slow and smooth.
Control on the way down — bell to the floor as cleanly as it came up. Closes the flow before switching sides.

sets.notes: **This is a continuous FLOW, not separate stations.** Move through the full chain on ONE side — dead clean → front squat → lateral lunge → bent press → tactical clean — letting each move feed the next, then repeat on the other side. About 2 reps' worth at each move. **~25-35lb throughout, 2 rounds. Light groove** — keep the leg components light (front squat + lateral lunge are leg work the day before Friday legs). (Canonical: kb-flow-dead-clean-press — the Bent Press Flow.)

sets.name: Skill + Mobility Maintenance — TGU Checkpoint Refresh + Bent Press + Windmill

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 35lb. 2 rounds. **🔆 Cue-focus refresh this week — the get-up is a series of positions, not a movement:**
- **PAUSE at every checkpoint** — roll to elbow → to hand → hip bridge → sweep the leg through → half-kneel → stand. Then reverse it through the same six, in order. Rushing a checkpoint is how the shoulder gets caught out of position
- **Eyes ON the bell at every checkpoint** — the head follows the bell, not the floor
- **The arm stays locked VERTICAL the whole way** — straight-arm overhead lockout, packed shoulder; the arm never bends and never drifts off vertical
- **Ribs down on the hip bridge** — the most common leak is arching the low back to get height
- **Slow is the standard.** If a checkpoint feels rushed, you're going too fast for the load — drop the bell before the bell drifts.

**Reflection:** can you stop dead at all six checkpoints, both directions, with the bell still? A get-up you can pause anywhere is a get-up you own.

**LOAD:** 25-35lb. 2 rounds. Light maintenance this week.
- **It's leverage, NOT a press** — the arm locks out by hinging your body DOWN under the bell
- **Hinge and rotate AWAY from the bell side**, eyes tracking the bell
- **The stretch lives in the bell-side hip + hamstring**, NOT the lower back — long spine
- Right shoulder watch — keep it stacked.

**LOAD:** 20-35lb. 2 rounds. Light maintenance this week.
- **Bell locked overhead, eyes track the bell** — the overhead arm never bends
- **Turn the feet ~45° away from the loaded side; hinge AWAY from the bell side** — lower the free hand toward the front foot
- **The stretch lives in the back-leg hip flexor + obliques, NOT the lower back** — long spine
- Slow descent, controlled return. Right shoulder watch.

sets.notes: Mobility maintenance — the TGU takes the cue-focus refresh this week (checkpoints, one at a time); bent press + windmill drop back to light maintenance. Sharp cues, light loads.

sets.name: Balance Closer — Single-Leg RDL + Bird-Dog + Standing Side-to-Side Twist

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 20-25lb. Single-leg balance + hip hinge. **The point is balance and control, not load** — keep it light so the legs stay fresh for Friday. Standing-leg glute locked, hips square, slow reach to the floor and back. The wobble is the training.
Bodyweight. Slow anti-rotation balance — opposite arm + leg extend, hold 2s, hips stay square (no rotation). Resets the spine after the single-leg work.

**LOAD:** 20-25lb (LIGHT — the straight-arm lever makes it feel heavy).
- **Stand tall, one bell held by the horns in BOTH hands, arms straight out in front** at chest height
- **Keep the arms straight and twist the bell side to side** — through center to one side, back through center to the other — bracing the core to control the rotation
- **Ribs down, stand tall** — the twist comes from the core/obliques, NOT the lower back
- Smooth and controlled, no momentum. No leg load — zero pre-fatigue for Friday.

sets.notes: Light balance + core close, 2 rounds, ~5 min. Move through the three back-to-back with short rest. Settles the system after the flow work before the cooldown.

exercises.notes: 60s each side. Hip flexor release — counters the TGU hip bridge and the lateral lunge work.
60s. Adductors get tight from the lateral lunges.

tips: **The press-to-march has left this day** — it's move #4 of the GymFiesta circuit, which now runs whole on Tuesday. Thursday gets its own coordination move instead of a borrowed one.
**Thursday carries heavy UPPER push** — fresh off Monday, doesn't tax Friday legs (a free second push exposure). Load the strict press / bent press; keep the LEGS light.
**Permanent Flow + Coordination block.** This week: figure-8 march — the weave you already own, now walked. The pass happens under a moving leg; exact hand-offs or the bell finds a shin.
**Skill novelty over intensity.** The win is the chain learned clean, not a cardio burn. Keep the bell light.

**Bent Press Flow is the canonical 5-move flow** — dead clean → front squat → lateral lunge → bent press → tactical clean. Light groove, 2 rounds, ~25-35lb (keep the leg components light before Friday legs).
**Strength block — strict press 50 at 8/8/8** (the reps you earned in W20) + rows 40. Strict, no push-press.
**Mobility maintenance = TGU checkpoint refresh** — pause at every one of the six checkpoints, both directions, eyes on the bell, arm locked vertical. Bent press + windmill drop to light maintenance.
**Bottoms-up press standard in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane (T-plane light).
**Balance closer, not a metabolic finisher** — single-leg RDL → bird-dog → standing side-to-side twist. Keeps the legs fresh for Friday.
**Right shoulder watch on the overhead work** — press, bent press, TGU. Lighten and slow down if it talks.
**Protective shrug greasing set in the warmup.**
Rotation plan: the Flow + Coordination block rotates content (W22 a halo → reverse lunge or a fresh weave); mobility maintenance cue-focus returns to the windmill.
formPhilosophy: Thursday keeps its permanent home for base KB skill + coordination, and this week it stops borrowing. The press-to-march goes back to the circuit it came from (now running whole on Tuesday) and the figure-8 march takes the slot on its own merits — the weave already owned, now made harder by adding locomotion rather than load. The mobility block turns its cue-focus to the get-up, which rewards patience more than any other move in the library: six checkpoints, each one a position you should be able to stop dead in. The strict press holds the 8s it earned. Thursday's identity holds: conditioning + skill + balance, legs kept light so Friday legs stays strong. Building decades, not weeks.
